newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate edges up to 9.1 from 7.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate edges up to 9.1 from 7.7 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate edged up to 9.1 pct on Friday from 7.7 pct propelled by growing demand for fresh kuna funds.
All supply of kuna funds at Zagreb money market was used and trade rose to 37.4 million kuna, at an average rate of 8.8 for call money. Dealers said banks' accounts were still thin.
One long-term loan was struck at 11.4 pct, and another six-10 day rate at 10.3 pct. Insurers rolled over previous loans at 7.0 pct.
Interbank loans were made at 12.0 pct.
Overnight trade totalled 31.0 million kuna, which the banks used to maintain their reserve payment.
The central bank calculaed its kuna midrate for the weekend and next Monday firmer at 5.4527 to the dollar and 3.5636 to the mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
